source: Dev-proposed semantic remap built from the official legacy->current mapping (answer tspi 25.07.2026.pdf) + module-file examples (H-001 Curcuma, H-006 BENCHAKUL). Requires domain-expert sign-off before any converted registry may enter production (Blocker 1 rule: mapping must be reviewed semantically, never a blind numeric shift).

conversion_types.EXACT_SEMANTIC_MAPPING: same concept, possibly renumbered; safe to auto-apply (Tier A)
conversion_types.RENAMED_REFINED: same concept, refined name; safe to auto-apply (Tier A)
conversion_types.SPLIT_REQUIRES_REVIEW: legacy axis split into several current axes; needs expert choice (Tier B)
conversion_types.CONTEXT_DEPENDENT: target current axis depends on the module's mechanism (Tier B)
conversion_types.SAME_NUMBER_DIFFERENT_MEANING: legacy number reused for a different concept; NEVER numeric-shift (Tier B)
conversion_types.DEPRECATED_TO_NETWORK: legacy 'axis' is actually a network in the new model (Tier C)
conversion_types.NO_DIRECT_EQUIVALENT: no current axis; quarantine for expert (Tier C)

match_by: legacy_name (semantic). legacy_number is advisory only and must not be used alone.

mappings.note: Legacy 'Metabolic Balance' is NOT current A27 (Glycation/Carbonyl Stress). Same number, different meaning — a numeric shift here is clinically wrong. Expert must choose the intended current axis (likely A5/A6/A7).
Legacy 19 'Cancer Surveillance' collides with current A18/A19 (gut). Maps into Oncology (A37/A38/A39) — expert must confirm which.
Bare 'Liver' maps to A35 (Visceral Organ Functional Reserve) only when the module's mechanism is organ-reserve; detox mechanisms map to A15. Depends on module mechanism.
Legacy Oncology splits into A37 Oncologic Cell Fate / A38 Tumor Microenvironment / A39 Genomic Regulation — expert selects.
Deprecated concept; folds under A10 Proteostasis–Autophagy–Lysosome (sub-axis A10A/B). Not a standalone axis in the new model.

CELA is NOT an axis. It is Network #120 under A34 (25 Jul client ruling). Convert as a network link, not an axis.
